description: Hand-written short technical documents for retrieval evaluation.

text: A B-tree keeps keys sorted so a database can find a row with a logarithmic number of disk reads instead of scanning every page.
title: B-tree indexes

text: Durability comes from recording each change in a log before the data pages are updated, so a crash can be recovered by replaying the log.
title: Write-ahead logging

text: Multiversion concurrency control lets readers see a consistent snapshot while writers create new row versions, avoiding read-write locks.
title: MVCC

text: A cost-based optimizer estimates how many rows each operator emits and picks the join order with the cheapest predicted total cost.
title: Query planners

text: Splitting rows across many machines by a partition key spreads load, at the cost of expensive queries that must touch several partitions.
title: Sharding

text: By slowly increasing the sending window and backing off when packets are lost, endpoints share a link without collapsing it.
title: TCP congestion control

text: Turning a hostname into an address walks a hierarchy of name servers, caching answers along the way to cut latency.
title: DNS resolution

text: Before encrypting traffic the two sides agree on a cipher and exchange keys, authenticating the server with a certificate.
title: TLS handshake

text: Response headers tell intermediaries how long a document may be reused, so repeat requests can be answered without contacting the origin.
title: HTTP caching

text: Spreading incoming connections across a pool of servers keeps any single machine from being overwhelmed and allows rolling restarts.
title: Load balancing

text: A keypair lets anyone encrypt with the public half while only the holder of the private half can decrypt, removing shared secrets.
title: Public key cryptography

text: A good digest maps any input to a fixed-size value such that finding two inputs with the same output is computationally infeasible.
title: Hash functions

text: Signing a message with a private key lets others verify, with the matching public key, that it was not altered and who produced it.
title: Digital signatures

text: Block ciphers transform fixed-size chunks under a shared key; a mode of operation chains blocks so identical plaintext differs.
title: Symmetric ciphers

text: Two parties can derive a shared secret over a public channel so an eavesdropper who sees every message still cannot compute the key.
title: Key exchange

text: Training nudges parameters in the direction that most reduces the loss, taking steps proportional to a learning rate.
title: Gradient descent

text: A model that memorizes its training set performs poorly on new data; regularization and more examples push it to generalize.
title: Overfitting

text: Sharing small filters across an image detects the same feature anywhere, drastically cutting parameters versus dense layers.
title: Convolutional networks

text: Instead of a fixed window, each position weighs every other position by relevance, letting a model relate distant tokens.
title: Attention mechanism

text: Mapping words to dense vectors places similar meanings near each other, so arithmetic on the vectors captures analogies.
title: Word embeddings

text: The operating system gives each process its own address space, paging rarely used memory to disk and mapping pages on demand.
title: Virtual memory

text: A scheduler decides which ready task runs next, balancing responsiveness for interactive jobs against throughput for batch work.
title: Process scheduling

text: Metadata structures track which disk blocks hold each file and keep directories, while journaling guards against corruption on crash.
title: File systems

text: When processes each hold a resource the other needs and refuse to release, none can proceed; detection or ordered acquisition avoids it.
title: Deadlock

text: A heap allocator carves blocks from a large region and tracks free space, trading fragmentation against speed of reuse.
title: Memory allocation

text: A managed runtime reclaims memory no longer reachable from the program, freeing developers from manual deallocation.
title: Garbage collection

text: Checking the kinds of values a program manipulates before it runs catches whole classes of mistakes without a single test case.
title: Type systems

text: A function that captures variables from the scope where it was defined carries that environment with it wherever it is later called.
title: Closures

text: A routine that calls itself on a smaller input solves problems defined in terms of themselves, provided a base case stops the descent.
title: Recursion

text: Locks, semaphores and channels coordinate threads so shared state is updated without races and work is handed off safely.
title: Concurrency primitives

text: Exposing resources behind predictable URLs and standard verbs lets clients and servers evolve independently over plain HTTP.
title: REST APIs

text: Upgrading an HTTP connection to a persistent, two-way channel lets a server push updates without the client polling repeatedly.
title: WebSockets

text: The engine parses markup into a tree, computes styles and layout, then paints pixels, re-running the steps when the page changes.
title: Browser rendering

text: Copying assets to servers near users cuts distance and load on the origin, so pages load faster worldwide.
title: Content delivery networks

text: If a site renders attacker-supplied text as markup, injected script runs with the victim's session; escaping output prevents it.
title: Cross-site scripting

text: Packaging an application with its dependencies in an isolated namespace makes it run the same on a laptop and in production.
title: Containers

text: Placing work on a durable queue lets producers and consumers run at different rates and survive one side being temporarily down.
title: Message queues

text: An operation that can be applied many times with the same effect as once lets a client safely retry after an uncertain failure.
title: Idempotency

text: Replicas that accept writes independently converge to the same state over time, trading immediate agreement for availability.
title: Eventual consistency

text: Capping how many requests a client may make in a window protects a service from overload and abusive traffic.
title: Rate limiting
